Class ForwardingLogProperties

java.lang.Object
io.jstach.rainbowgum.properties.ForwardingLogProperties
All Implemented Interfaces:
LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable
public abstract class ForwardingLogProperties extends Object implements LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable
Properties that forward every lookup to a delegate, for writing decorators that observe or change lookups.

valueOrNull(String), listOrNull(String), mapOrNull(String), visit(String, BiFunction), description(String), order(), and report(Appendable) forward to delegate(). When the delegate's visit passes the delegate itself to the visitor, this properties is passed instead, so lookups that go through visit, such as LogProperties.forKey(String), reach the methods of this properties. The other methods are the LogProperties defaults, which are built on these.

    • listOrNull

      public @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key)
      Description copied from interface: LogProperties
      Gets a list or null if the key is missing and by default uses LogProperties.parseList(String). The default implementation will parse the string value as a list using LogProperties.parseList(String) but custom implementations may rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing configuration system.

      The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated and percent-encoded ( application/x-www-form-urlencoded) for entries needing to contain the separator or an equals sign, for example: 

      logging.appenders=console,file
      resolves to ["console", "file"], and: 
      logging.appenders=one%20two,three%2Cfour
      (a space and an escaped comma) resolves to ["one two", "three,four"]. See LogProperties.parseList(String) for empty elements.
      Specified by:
      listOrNull in interface LogProperties
      Parameters:
      key - property name.
      Returns:
      list or null.

    • mapOrNull

      public @Nullable Map<String,String> mapOrNull(String key)
      Description copied from interface: LogProperties
      Gets a map or null if the key is missing and by default uses LogProperties.parseMap(String). The default implementation will parse the string value as map using LogProperties.parseMap(String) but custom implementations may rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing configuration system.

      The returned map must iterate in a stable order, the same every time for the same configuration, preferably the order its entries were declared.

      The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated key=value pairs, percent-encoded ( application/x-www-form-urlencoded) for entries needing to contain the separator or an equals sign, for example: 

      logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=environment=prod,region=us-east
      resolves to {"environment": "prod", "region": "us-east"}, and: 
      logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=region=us%20east
      (a percent-encoded space) resolves to {"region": "us east"}.

      When that property is not set, the map can instead be given as a list of its keys in key.keys and each value in key.mapKey, which works with sources that only hold flat values such as system properties or environment variables, keeps the declared order, and needs no encoding: 

      logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.keys=environment,region
logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.environment=prod
logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.region=us east
      A key listed without a value is an error.
      Specified by:
      mapOrNull in interface LogProperties
      Parameters:
      key - property name.
      Returns:
      map or null.

    • visit

      public <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key, BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor)
      Description copied from interface: LogProperties
      Visits this properties with visitor, by default just applying visitor to this and key directly. A composite/aggregate LogProperties (one backed by more than one underlying source) overrides this to recursively visit each of its members in order, returning the first non-null result - which member actually produced it is exactly what visitor is handed as its first argument, so a composite never needs to know anything about what visitor is trying to build (a raw value, a resolved property, or anything else); it just walks its members and stops at the first hit.
      Specified by:
      visit in interface LogProperties
      Type Parameters:
      R - result type.
      Parameters:
      key - property key.
      visitor - applied to (the member of this properties that ends up handling the visit, key); a null return means keep visiting.
      Returns:
      first non-null result, or null if nothing visited produced one.
